lessons.title: Making an appointment
lessons.goal: Make, confirm and cancel an appointment on the phone.

tip.title: Polite: Könnten Sie …?
tip.body: On the phone, polite forms help a lot: Könnten Sie das bitte wiederholen? Separable verbs split: absagen → Ich sage den Termin ab. Note halb zehn means 9:30 (half to ten). End phone calls with Auf Wiederhören, not Auf Wiedersehen. Speak a little slower than usual and say your name clearly.

lessons.title: Problems and complaints
lessons.goal: Report a problem, complain politely and ask for a solution.

tip.title: Complain politely
tip.body: Start softly with leider (unfortunately) and say how long the problem has lasted with seit + dative: Die Heizung ist seit Montag kaputt. Ich hätte gern … is a polite way to ask for what you want. Ei sounds like English 'eye' and z like 'ts': HEI-tsung.

lessons.title: Reflexive verbs: mich, dich, sich
lessons.goal: Use sich melden, sich freuen and other reflexive verbs.

tip.title: The pronoun matches the subject
tip.body: Reflexive verbs need a pronoun that matches the subject: ich freue mich, du freust dich, er/sie freut sich, wir freuen uns, Sie freuen sich. On the phone you often hear: Ich melde mich morgen. sich freuen auf + accusative means to look forward to something.

lessons.title: Leave a voicemail
lessons.goal: Leave a clear phone message for 40 seconds.

culture.title: Phone etiquette: Müller am Apparat
culture.body: Germans often answer the phone with just their surname — Müller? or Müller, guten Tag — and offices say the company name plus their own surname. End calls with Auf Wiederhören ("until we hear again"). In Switzerland a mobile is often called a Natel and a bike a Velo; in Germany and Austria it is Handy and Fahrrad (Radl in the south).
